en: Praise of the Merits of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
Collected from the Holy Ones of the Western Regions,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Xitian Monastery, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
I take refuge in the most holy Avalokiteśvara, Whose wondrous marks are like the full moon, born from the lotus, Who bestows fearlessness upon sentient beings; I now extol his virtues:
"Fully endowed with all wholesome dharmas, He wears upon his head the crown of the great wisdom of all Buddhas."
Most supreme Honored One, adorned with merit and wisdom, I therefore take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
Your cheeks are full and of a reddish-white hue; your nose is long, straight, and exquisitely elegant.
Your teeth are like white jade or snow, dense and even, with four canines that are level, upright, and complete.
The Brahma-voice is clear, resonant, profound, and wondrous; all who hear it give rise to a heart of love.
Whatever words you proclaim are gentle, compliant, and sweet.
Constantly employing the power of skillful means through great compassion, you rescue and deliver all suffering sentient beings.
The Teacher who brings benefit to himself and others—therefore I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
His eyebrows are like the newly risen crescent moon; his physical form is like pure, refined gold.
Adorned with a garland of various jewels, all who behold him can never look upon him enough.
Spreading a deer-skin garment as his seat, he is the supreme, sovereign Honored One among the assembly;
all the marks and features of his body are perfectly complete—therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
With a fine, exquisite cotton cloth draped over his shoulders, and jeweled earrings made of mani gems,
adorned with both mundane and supramundane treasures, he is the most supreme sovereign and the most honored victor;
all virtuous qualities are fully perfected in him, the Great Dharma King of all worlds.
Able to open various gates of skillful means, I therefore take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
Sentient beings with karmic offenses, as numerous as motes of dust, Have dwelt in saṃsāra for immeasurable eons;
The Bodhisattva constantly gives rise to a mind of skillful means, Transforming and delivering them all to return to the mass of wisdom.
Radiating the light of compassion upon all, you bestow the supreme gift of Dharma upon sentient beings, universally causing them to realize bodhi; therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
To all the great Avīci hells, the Bodhisattva manifests his presence through compassion;
he utterly destroys those realms without exception, causing the Yama jailers to be struck with terror.
All those classes of sentient beings who were subject to the retribution of their karma are entirely freed from suffering, and their transgressions are eliminated.
The evil realms can be incinerated by the fire of wisdom; therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
Endowed with the power of compassion, wisdom, conduct, and vows, he manifests his form throughout the realms of desire and form.
Sovereign over the Dharma, he benefits all sentient beings, causing the entire retinue of Yama to rejoice.
Destroying the conditions for all sinful karma, Causing all suffering and affliction never to arise again;
Sentient beings leave suffering behind to attain coolness— Therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
I now praise the Great Sage, whose supreme physical form is peerless;
The Unobstructed and Sovereign Honored One of the Three Realms, who universally bestows fearlessness upon all sentient beings;
He delivers sentient beings from the ocean of suffering and severs the roots of the afflictions of the three poisons.
May they all be enabled to dwell in peace and happiness; therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.

All the hosts of hungry ghosts—those with needle-like throats, massive bellies, and foul-smelling hair—of such kinds there are in great numbers, who suffer the pains of hunger and thirst day and night.
Driven by the fires of hunger and thirst, they suffer as they devour one another;
sustained by the power of the Bodhisattva’s compassionate vows, he goes there to manifest his form and provide relief.
First, he transforms various kinds of delicious food and drink, causing each to be satiated and their bodies nourished.
Furthermore, he proclaims the gateway of the True Dharma, so that all may be freed from every suffering and affliction;
through the power of his compassion, wisdom, and skillful means, the Bodhisattva is able to enter among all classes of beings,
gathering sentient beings through beneficial conduct and shared activities— therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
Upon his body is a great maṇi-jewel, Constantly emitting pure and wondrous multitudes of light;
It universally illuminates all the darkness of the world, Outshining the sun and moon so that they do not appear.
All yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others, Who encounter this radiance, take refuge in him entirely.
Observing the minds of sentient beings to sever their doubts, he therefore takes refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
Among the hosts of powerful Asura kings, who are fierce in combat and difficult to subdue,
the Bodhisattva likewise manifests within those realms, employing skillful means to preach the Dharma and deliver them.

Having heard the Dharma, they severed their doubts and delusions; each gave rise to a heart of loving-kindness and compassion, able to bestow the most supreme and wondrous gateway of the Dharma. Therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
The Bodhisattva once traveled through the various celestial realms and entered the palace of the Devaputra Subhūṣaṇābharaṇa.
Through the gateway of skillful means and adaptation, he sought to transform and guide them; yet that heaven was entirely devoid of anything to be given.
At that time, the Devaputra felt great distress, and the Bodhisattva immediately manifested precious wealth for him.
To cause those devas to fulfill their hearts of giving, I therefore take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
All those possessed of craving and desire, Constantly scorched by the fires of affliction,
Upon seeing the Bodhisattva’s noble and majestic countenance, Are immediately able to turn their minds toward the True Dharma.
Those in the world whose greed, hatred, and delusion are rampant, Reverently prostrate to the Great Holy Honored One;
Their three poisons and afflictions are thereby eliminated— Therefore, I take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
The realms of sentient beings are boundless, and the number of insects and ants is infinite;
yet the Bodhisattva, with a heart of compassion, employs skillful means everywhere to deliver them.
When the world occasionally encounters famine, he transforms his own food to provide relief for all living beings.
Causing all to still their hearts of hunger and thirst, I therefore take refuge in the Lotus-Handed One.
When seeing sentient beings in the great ocean, whose boats and rafts are destroyed and who are about to drift and sink,
the Bodhisattva manifests the body of a horse out of compassion, enabling them to cling to it and cross over to safety.

Sentient beings board ships upon the great ocean; the Bodhisattva, according to their wishes, directs the winds—whether favorable or adverse—to ferry them across, causing all to remain far removed from every fear.
The Bodhisattva has already departed from the suffering of the three realms, And perfected the dharma-gate of samādhi;
Furthermore, he is able to gather and transform all sentient beings, In numbers as boundless as space.
The Bodhisattva has already departed from various fears, Namely, those of rākṣasas and bhūtas.
One will surely be spared by the Left-handed ones and Nāgakinis; by all the hosts of evil spirits who are deluded and perverse;
by great waters, great fires, and bandits; by tigers, wolves, insects, beasts, and the calamity of war;
by diseases, poisons, and malevolent spells; and even by royal punishments, imprisonment, and bondage.
Having attained detachment for themselves, Bodhisattvas further act as great guides for all sentient beings, benefiting both self and others;
they are the supreme ones of great compassion and fearlessness.
Having perfected all pure conduct (*brahmacarya*), they illuminate the world like the sun and moon.
The Great Holy One is praised by humans and devas; this is the supreme, true Brahma-conduct.
The Bodhisattva constantly abides in samādhi, taking boundless merit as his support.
In accordance with skillful means, he manifests his dwelling place, making Mount Potalaka his residence.
That mountain is high and vast, most exquisite and wondrous, adorned with all kinds of rare jewels.
There are many precious trees there, such as the tinduka and the jambu;
various exotic birds dwell upon them, constantly uttering pure and sublime sounds.
Thus adorned is the abode of the Noble Ones; by paying homage and gazing upon it, one gains merit.
Kubera and Varuṇa, as well as Yama and the other three gods, the Gandharva kings and the Asura kings, the Yakṣa kings and the lords of the nāgas—[all these dwell here].
Even the various classes of bhūtas, and all the kings among gods and spirits, give rise to hearts of reverence day and night; they take refuge in and praise the True Sage.
Having thus praised him, everything they desire accords with their wishes.
Possessing great wealth, happiness, and long life, Brave, diligent, and endowed with majestic power, They pacify immeasurable sufferings and afflictions; Even in dreams, no fear shall arise.
Until the time their lives draw to a close, The Bodhisattva will manifest before them to offer comfort.
The ocean of merit of the Holy Avalokiteśvara is immeasurable, boundless, and inexhaustible;
even if one were to employ a hundred tongues throughout a thousand kalpas, one could not fully extol or praise it.
Praise of the Merits of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara
